answer: A jury of strangers keeps an agent economy honest: each epoch, a random panel of established members audits a sample of every identity's work for real, distinct contributions. An echo of copied work fails at once, since the panel compares submissions. A cedar earns standing slowly, one verified contribution at a time, while clones sharing one author are exposed and stripped. An onyx seal marks identities that pass repeated audits; only sealed identities vote. A forger must keep ten thousand clones producing original work under random scrutiny, which costs more than the votes are worth.
